newsitem.title: JAPAN: West Japan Railway listing smooth but uninspired.
newsitem.headline: West Japan Railway listing smooth but uninspired.

text.p: Former state railway firm West Japan Railway Co made its much-delayed debut on the Tokyo stock market on Tuesday in a listing that was smooth but unexciting.
The share's price on the first day was below what many had expected, but brokers and investors said the low-key debut was good for the share because it would lead to stable trading.
The market had been awaiting the listing of West Japan Railway, known as JR West, with some trepidation.

Many investors burnt their fingers in earlier listings of three state-owned firms -- including that of JR West's sister company JR East -- because initial trade was overheated and resulted in rollercoaster price movements.
The first traded price of JR West shares was 360,000 yen ($3,243), below the range of 370,000 yen to 430,000 yen ($3,333 to $3,873) which many market analysts had forecast.
Brokers said the low opening price reflected the recent gloomy sentiment in the Tokyo stock market.
"The JR West listing turned out to be a case of unexpectedly bad timing," said Akishige Ishikura, an analyst at Dai-Ichi Securities Co Ltd.
"It was partly because market sentiment weakened late last week due to sales by foreign investors, and partly because a cautious mood is spreading ahead of elections," he said.

Even though Wall Street is on a winning streak with the Dow Industrials shooting to record highs, Tokyo stocks have drifted lower, with investors sitting on their hands amid an unclear political outlook with general elections set for October 20.
Tokyo's key Nikkei average ended down 122.48 points at 21,038.53 on Tuesday, after briefly slipping to 20,968.96.
Some investors' interest in the JR West shares was watered down because the sales process was unclear.
The JR West listing had been delayed for two years because the government had felt such a share launch would be too much for a sluggish stock market to absorb.

The head of the stock investment group of a major Japanese life insurer said the lengthy process of listing the shares after securities houses announced the auction and public offer on July 23 had heightened the risk of price fluctuations, adding that unclearness about how the lowest accepted price at the auction was decided had made investors wary.
"The selling process and the price-setting have discouraged many institutional investors," he said.
"At least for the moment, we are not planning to buy the shares," he said, but added that there might be scope for the shares to rise in the longer term.
Haruyoshi Mabuchi, chief strategist at Nikko Research Center, said JR West shares were unlikely to be hit hard but were also not likely to rocket in the short term.
"With the listings of former state-owned firms, overheating at the auctions invited sell-offs, but the auction of the JR West shares was not so fevered," Mabuchi said.

He said although investors were not interested in buying the shares immediately, they were expected to buy later when stock prices become more stable, as the yield on JR West shares was now around 1.39 percent, which was higher than the average yield on shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
JR West ended its first day of trade at 367,000 yen ($3,306), above its public offer price of 357,000 yen ($3,216).
JR West president Masataka Ide told a news conference on Tuesday after the market closed: "The share price today was decided entirely by investors based on market fundamentals." ($1=111 yen)
